title: Ramp-to-steady-state experimentation, benchmark methodology, and customer acceptance criteria
creator: Maya Patel
description: Objective: build and validate a ramp-to-steady-state load harness and benchmarking methodology that measures realistic sustained throughput for Dedicated capacity, informs autoscaler hysteresis and burst policies, and produces deterministic acceptance criteria customers can use to sign off on capacity purchases. Scope includes: scenario generator, tenant-mix emulator, KV-cache priming, cold/warm start characterization, sustained tail-latency profiling (p50/p95/p99), throughput degradation modes, and automated acceptance report generation for customers. Deliverables: 1) Load harness repo and runner templates (tenant-mix JSONs, sequence-length distributions, tokenization mix), 2) Benchmark methodology doc with reproducible steps and failure modes, 3) Acceptance checklist and pass/fail criteria for customer signoff, 4) Calibration patterns for autoscaler (scale up/down thresholds, cooldowns) and fleet controls (fallback routing, degraded-model policy), 5) Grafana dashboards and a reproducible CSV summary for each run. Non-goals: microbenchmarks of single-GPU perf kernels (covered elsewhere), long-term degradation studies beyond 7-day runs.

acceptance_criteria: Steady-state defined and reproducible: run includes a linear ramp from 0% to target over 10 minutes, hold for 30 minutes (+/- 5%), then linear ramp-down over 10 minutes; metrics recorded at 10s resolution.
Throughput gating: observed sustained token throughput over the hold period >= 95% of target for >90% of 30-minute window (measured at 1-minute buckets).
Tail latency SLOs: p95 latency during hold <= configured SLO (default 350ms), p99 <= 2x SLO. Any p99 spikes must have a traceable root cause (GC, cache miss, kernel swap).
Cache priming requirement: run with and without KV-cache priming; delta must be documented and used to recommend recommended priming steps for customers.
Autoscaler behavior: no more than 2 scale actions within any 5-minute sliding window when holding; scale-up completes within configured scale_up_window (target 60s).

Graceful degradation: when throughput exceeds capacity by >15%, system must return configured 503 + explanatory header for degraded requests and trigger fallback routing to pre-configured reduced-cost model variant within 150ms of decision.

Tenant isolation: in mixed-tenant runs, no single synthetic tenant may consume >40% of capacity unless explicitly configured in scenario; violations must generate an alert and be logged to audit stream.
Reproducible report: automated runbook produces a CSV summary, a one-page pass/fail report, and attached Grafana dashboard links suitable for customer signoff.
run_playbook: Setup: provision dedicated-staging cluster with equal node types and patch level runtime-1.22; enable precise telemetry (token counts, queue lengths, per-tenant metrics).
Priming: run KV-cache priming script for 20 minutes at 10% of target traffic; verify cache hit-rate >80% before ramp.
Ramp: start linear ramp from 0 to target over 10 minutes using tenant-mix JSON (default-mix.json) with token distribution matching customer profile.
Hold: maintain target for 30 minutes; collect p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU util, memory, queue depths, and autoscaler events. Trigger a synthetic tenant spike at minute 15 to validate isolation.
Ramp-down: linear ramp down over 10 minutes; verify no residual throttles or stuck requests.
Post-run: run automated analyzer to produce pass/fail gates and an annotated timeline of incidents. Attach CSV and Grafana links to customer report.
